name: Modify: change a field in an existing EMD entry
description: Update one or several JSON fields in any existing src-data file (opens a PR for review)
title: [EMD] Modify: [do not edit]

field_guidance.folder:
**Data folder**

Pick the folder that contains the file you want to change.

If you're not sure which folder a given entry lives in, browse `src-data` on GitHub.
field_guidance.filename:
**Existing filename**

The `@id` of the file you want to change. With or without the trailing `.json` — the handler will add it if missing.

**Example:** for `model/canesm5-1.json` enter `canesm5-1`.

If the file does not exist the submission will fail.
field_guidance.key:
**Field name**

The JSON key to update. Nested keys are supported with dot notation, e.g. `metadata.version`.

**The key must already exist on the file** — if it does not, the submission will fail. Use the relevant stage form to add new fields.

Leave this blank if you are changing several fields via **Changes**.
field_guidance.value:
**New value**

Write the new value as you want it to appear in the JSON. Examples:

- A string: `My new description`
- A list: `["https://doi.org/...", "https://doi.org/..."]`
- A number: `2024`
- A boolean: `true`
- An object: `{"key": "value"}`

If the value parses as JSON it is stored as that type; otherwise it is kept as a string.
field_guidance.changes:
**Changing several fields at once**

A JSON object mapping field names to their new values:

```json
{
  "n_cells": 220509,
  "southernmost_latitude": -85.3556519090144,
  "description": "The horizontal grid spacing varies locally between about 10 and 120 km."
}
```

Values keep their JSON type, so quote strings and leave numbers and booleans bare. Nested keys work with dot notation, e.g. `"metadata.version": "2.1"`.

Every key must already exist on the file. They are checked before anything is written, so if one is wrong nothing changes and you can fix it and resubmit.

Use this **or** **Field name** / **New value**, never both.

Prefer this whenever one correction spans several fields. All the changes then land in a single commit, so the entry is never published in a part-updated state, and the reviewer sees the whole correction at once instead of a fragment of it.
field_guidance.justification:
**Why this change?**

A short explanation that reviewers can use to decide whether to approve. Be specific about what was wrong before and why the new value is correct — cite a paper, a release note, or a model card if you can.
